findings.title: Do not rebind historical PASS reviews to a different source
findings.problem: All six signed PASS records change sourceKey from d08068088a65eaa73598f59d to d3171877122dfc6376c52399 while retaining their October 29 review dates, results, and report references. This asserts approval for a different source without supplying a review of that source. Re-signing the edited metadata does not establish that the adversary reviewed it. The unchanged diagram keys might indicate equivalent rendered content, but the renderer/hash implementation and any equivalence verification are not supplied, so I could not verify that justification.
findings.failure_scenario: When the current source no longer matches the source covered by the historical reviews, replacing the freshness binding makes those old PASS results appear current. The accompanying item-map is also rebound and re-signed, and the new pairing report lists 678 shipped pairings. If the source change affects any rendered clinical detail, students can receive visuals not covered by the referenced adversarial reviews.
findings.fix: Keep the historical source bindings intact. Review the current rendered source through the visual adversarial gate and generate the signed index/map from those results. If this is an unchanged-render migration, provide machine-verifiable equivalence evidence through the existing approval process rather than simply rewriting historical approval metadata.

assessment: One blocking approval-provenance concern: historical visual-review passes are reassigned to a new source digest without corresponding review evidence. The diagram pairings and clinical values themselves are unchanged.
